The function you provided does not deal with the range of cells the results are written to. The range defines where the results are displayed and is usually set in Excel, not within the function itself.

However, if you do want to change the range where the data is displayed, you can typically click on the cell in the upper-left corner where your formula is and drag the selection to the desired range. In this case, you would click on AB38 and drag to NW35.

It's worth mentioning, that your current CMPGetResults function might only result in a single column of data because of the parameters that have been set (row_offset 2 & col_offset -1). The desired range you've specified (AB26:NW35) is of a significant size, so you might want to adjust these parameters accordingly to fill the entire range.

Please, consult the developer or the manual of the CMPGetResults and CMPCalcs function for in-depth instructions as these formulas aren't standard Excel functions and appear to be custom or add-in based, and without being familiar with the specifics of these functions, it's hard to suggest a precise edit.
